Ironman concerns | 40 Smithing [ boostable ] (to make the gold bar if not dropped by a monster) or 33 Magic [ boostable ] (to telegrab a gold bar from Varrock west bank basement) or 5 Thieving to steal from a crafting stall in Keldagrim. A gold bar is also a reward from The Digsite , Goblin Diplomacy , and Waterfall Quest

League notes | Unlocking Kandarin ✓ will auto-complete the quest

Ape Atoll is one of the most dangerous areas in the game. All native creatures other than the level 5 birds will be aggressive towards you, regardless of your combat level , whenever you're not wearing the monkey greegree (made later in the quest). Players can hug the coasts of Ape Atoll when moving to avoid the poisonous snakes and spiders; some snakes may still be encountered this way, but players can simply wait for them to move.

When going to the island, make sure to bring plenty of food , antipoison potions , and an emergency teleport , in addition to any other required items. Switching off auto retaliate and utilising protection prayers will greatly improve your chances of survival.

At any point, you can teleport or flee from Ape Atoll to restock items without losing your progress. To leave the island by boat, simply talk to Lumdo in the landing area to go from Ape Atoll back to Crash Island , and then talk to Waydar on Crash Island to go back to the Tree Gnome Stronghold . To resume the quest, talk to Daero on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree to go back to the hangar, talk to Waydar in the hangar to go back to Crash Island, and finally, talk to Lumdo on Crash Island to return to Ape Atoll.

| New Chapter

The jingle that plays upon starting a new chapter of the quest.

"In which our hero/heroine finds himself/herself/themself drawn back into Glough's web of deception and deceit."

Talk to King Narnode Shareen in the Tree Gnome Stronghold. He will tell you to investigate Glough 's old shipyard for any trace of the missing 10th Squad, and will give you the gnome royal seal . Bring this to Karamja (the "Gandius" option on the glider at the top of the Grand Tree will bring you nearby). If you do not have monkey bones (or a monkey corpse ), kill a monkey while on Karamja to obtain some.

Note: If you leave the quest to do something else, you will need the gnome royal seal to get into the shipyard

After arriving, enter the shipyard north of the glider landing site and speak with G.L.O. Caranock , a gnome officer for the shipyard. He can be found in the building in the southern area, near the fence. He will act very suspiciously when spoken to, and advise you to return to the king.

Return to King Narnode, and he will give you Narnode's orders and tell you to speak to Daero , the new head tree guardian. Daero can be found on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of the Grand Tree, near Blurberry Bar . Go through all the chat options with Daero, and ensure you're ready for surviving Ape Atoll; when you're ready, tell him you're prepared to leave. He will then blindfold you and take you to an underground hangar .

Talk to Daero in the hangar and he will introduce you to Waydar , a gnome pilot. Waydar will task you with solving a "reinitialisation" puzzle, which is similar to the puzzle boxes from Treasure Trails . If you have done these puzzles before, the sliding puzzle will be easy to complete; if not, see below for the solution, or bring 200,000 coins and go to Glough , who resides in the same area he did during the Grand Tree quest.

Begin solving the puzzle by clicking on the panel to the south-east by the southern glider. Players can take some spare controls from the nearby crate to view the solution, or simply consult the image below.

Solve the sliding puzzle as follows (with the piece numbers counting from the top left corner, moving left to right):

Manoeuvre pieces 1, 2, and 3 into their proper positions in the upper left corner. Position piece 4 in the upper right corner. Position piece 5 under piece 4 (shuffle pieces 4 and 5 around with some others if they are not in the right order). Slide piece 4 to the left and piece 5 up; the first row will now be done. Repeat this process with second and then third rows, leaving the completed rows intact. With rows 1-3 completed, the puzzle should now be solved in terms of 2-piece high columns. Position pieces 16 and 21 next to each other, in that order, on the right-hand side of the bottom row. Slide the remaining tiles clockwise to put them in place. Repeat this process with pieces 17 and 22, then with pieces 18 and 23. Pieces 19, 20, and 24 should now be easily moved to their correct places.

After completing the puzzle, talk to Daero, and then Waydar. The two of you will depart and then land on the aptly named Crash Island , where the 10th Squad also crashed earlier. Ask the nearby sailor Lumdo to bring you to Ape Atoll , and he will refuse due to conflicting orders from his sergeant, Garkor ; since Lumdo says he will not take orders from you, talk to Waydar again instead (watch out for poisonous scorpions just to his left, and do not click "Travel", as this will bring you back to the Grand Tree). After speaking with Waydar, speak with Lumdo once more, and he will now agree to take you to Ape Atoll.

Do not click the 'X' to close the story tablet that shows up after this conversation or it will cancel the subsequent cut-scene and you'll have to go through the chat option again.

 | Meanwhile.

The jingle that plays upon a cutscene plays.

"In which our hero/heroine finds themselves engaging in severe quantities of monkey business."

Once on the Atoll, start going west, sticking to the southern coastline until you reach a mahogany tree. From here, run north, avoiding the poisonous snakes , scorpions , and jungle spiders . If you have the level to use it, activate Protect from Missiles as you travel north, as a volley of poisoned arrows will start pelting you as you come closer to the Ape Atoll gate. Once you get close enough to the entrance, you will be knocked out and placed in a prison.

After waking up, you will find yourself in a cell guarded by Trefaji and Aberab , two gorilla guards. Speak to Lumo , one of the captured 10th Squad members, and then prepare to make your escape.

Throughout this section and any time you are re-jailed, you will need to stay one square away from the northern cell wall (near the patrolling guards' path) if the guards are in front of it. If you're in their range, they will punch you for 10-20 damage. The guards follow a path, which is as follows: one of the guards will patrol the area twice, walking the length of the prison each time, and then leave to rotate shifts. Use the time that the guard moves away from your jail door to pick the lock. Once out, as the patrolling guard is walking out to switch with the one on standby, walk behind him to reach the exit. Be prepared to make several attempts.

After successfully making it out of the building, travel north of the jail and then east to find Karam , an assassin and member of the 10th Squad. Karam can be found in the bushes near the crafting shop ( ); he is mostly translucent and he can be difficult to spot, so look carefully. After finding him, speak with him to learn about the gnome mage Zooknock .

Refer to the map to the right for relevant locations during the quest. Be wary of all yellow dots, as they represent poisonous enemies (scorpions, snakes, and spiders), as well as aggressive monkey archers. When you are in the grass, the monkey archers do not fire, but it's still a good idea to activate Protect from Missiles as a precaution.

Once you're ready, travel south, past the large door, while staying in the tall jungle grass. Past the door, go around the castle counter-clockwise until you're at the southern end, and from here, run south-east, until you are between a white building and the castle. To the east of that building is Garkor , the Sergeant of the 10th Squad. Speak with him, and make sure to get all the way through the dialogue to the point where he tells you to go meet Zooknock in person.

Sprint west through the grass with Protect from Missiles on. Continue west (south of the buildings) in the grass until you reach the doorway to your north, marked on the map image above. Walk through the door to enter an enclosed area with a sleeping monkey guard, a banana crate , and a dentures crate .

When inside this house, stay on the dark brown ground along the walls , or you'll risk being sent back to jail. The spiders inside are poisonous, but their poison only hits 1 damage, so it might be helpful to save your anti-poisons for later in the quest. There are bananas in the south-western crates next to the ladder if the player needs a source of food.

From the entrance, head east and then north, and search the stacked crates towards the middle of the room to acquire monkey dentures . The sleeping guard is a non-threat so long as you don't talk to him; otherwise, he will call for guards.

After you have the dentures, search the south-easternmost crate and a prompt will appear, asking if you're ready to enter the area below. You will take 32.9% of your current hitpoints as fall damage if you drop down into the cavern when entering, so heal up if necessary before attempting it to avoid dying to the poisonous spiders. Your Agility level has a chance to negate this damage, so a summer pie or other Agility boost may help avoid fall damage during this section.

Once inside the cavern, travel to the north-west part of the area and search the crates to acquire the m'amulet mould . At this point, if you need to resupply, you can exit the city by going to the south-east corner of Marim , running past the guards and the gravedigger, and climbing up the ladder. After climbing up, jump off the bridge, and go back to the boat to Crash Island . You can also teleport out.

section_path: Monkey Business > Chapter 2 > The Light at the End of the Tunnel
text:
Note: Strange fruit are handy for this section as they also cure poison. You will spend about 220% total run energy to traverse to the end of the tunnel at minimum weight, with no energy conserving mechanics; bring enough energy restore to accommodate.

It is highly recommended to teleport out and bank at this point. This section involves running past dozens of accurate monkey zombies and gorilla skeletons which can hit up to 7 and 12 respectively, all while inside a long and tight multicombat tunnel. Ironmen or other accounts who don't have access to energy or prayer potions are advised to use other prayer-boosting items , in order to reduce prayer drain. Refer to the table below for the various threats faced throughout the dungeon.

Entrance Monkey Zombie, lvl 98 Skeleton, lvl 142 Zooknock

When you're ready, travel back to the southern part of Ape Atoll from the Gnome Hangar by speaking to Daero in the Grand Tree. Once you arrive, head west of Lumdo , and enter the tunnel ( ) below.

As soon as you enter, you'll see the screen will start to shake. Rumbling noises will play, and rocks will begin to fall; until you reach the tunnel, you are at constant risk of taking damage. Use the map to the right to navigate the dungeon.

Even with consistent running, it will take at least three minutes of running to navigate the dungeon. Be prepared to drink your prayer and energy restoring potions, as well as food, when necessary.

At the end of the tunnel, you will find the gnomes Zooknock , Waymottin and Bunkwicket . Talk to Zooknock, and then use your m'amulet mould , gold bar , and monkey dentures on him and speak to him again. Make sure he gives you an enchanted bar before leaving the tunnel . Additionally, do not to use the m'amulet mould on Zooknock when you already have the enchanted bar , as he will keep the mould and you will have to obtain another. Teleport out, and bank if necessary. If you have not gone through all the dialogue with Garkor you will not be able to use the items on him.

section_path: Monkey Business > Chapter 2 > Amulet of Monkeyspeak
text:
Note : If you are going to do Recipe for Disaster , bring a ranged or magic weapon to kill a monkey guard and archer to save time later. Low level Ironmen can use rune spear (kp) from Tai Bwo Wannai Trio if the healing is too much to handle.

After restocking, return to Ape Atoll and continue north-west until you are placed in the jail cell again. Escape the cell as before, then travel east towards the temple.

You must now descend through the trapdoor to the east in the temple (see map). Activate Protect from Melee before entering the temple to block attacks from the powerful monkey guards .

Most of the guards can simply be run through, but the ones with beards near the trapdoor will act as walls, trapping you if they surround you. The easiest method to get past the bearded gorillas is to go upstairs, and then climb down the ladder on the east side to get close to the trapdoor. If you choose to walk to the ladder directly, make sure to wait until the guards walk away; players can hide in the north-east corner of the temple until there is enough room to descend. If you're surrounded by guards and can't move, teleport out immediately; if you're trapped near the ladder, go up the stairs and hop worlds. Note that the ladder near the trap door can only be climbed up from the EAST side.

Go down the trapdoor while still praying against melee. Ignore the monkey zombies (or kill one and pick up the bones if you want to do Recipe for Disaster later), and swiftly use the enchanted bar on the nearby wall of flames to make an unstrung monkey amulet . Either travel back up the ladder or find a safespot to get away from the foes, and use the ball of wool with the unstrung amulet to create the full m'speak amulet . Be aware that if you ascend the ladder, you will be attacked and can be trapped as before, so ensure Protect from Melee is active.

section_path: Monkey Business > Chapter 2 > A Monkey's Uncle
text:
Head to the building west of the jail, making sure to sneak through the grass. You'll see a banana garden that has a Monkey Child in it, which is being patrolled by The Monkey's Aunt . The aunt follows a predetermined path, which loops around the wooden house by the garden; do not enter the garden when the monkey's aunt is present, or she will call for guards to arrest you. Note that if you're caught, you can sometimes escape without being arrested by quickly climbing up the ladder in the building nearby before the monkeys reach you. Do not speak to The Monkey's Uncle upstairs, as he will also call the guards. You can use the abandoned building next to the banana garden to quickly access the garden, as it has a connecting corridor out of sight.

Wait for the aunt to walk away, then speak to the monkey child, and tell him that you are his uncle. After he reveals that he is supposed to collect 20 bananas , search and pick five bananas from the nearby trees. The monkey cannot count, so you do not necessarily need 20, as long as you give him at least 5. Give him the bananas, then wait for a few moments in the corridor, and return to the monkey child when the aunt is away. Ask the child to lend you his monkey talisman .

You can obtain more than one talisman without dropping your current ones, so be sure to get an additional talisman for each greegree you want (four in total are needed for all quests; see below). You will need to speak to the monkey child again for each one, telling him you have lost the talisman, which will cause him to cry. Waiting for the aunt to pass by the child again will make the monkey child have another talisman available; Alternatively, you can switch worlds to potentially make the process go faster. If you talk to the child again before the aunt has passed by, you will get the message "The monkey child is too busy crying..."

text:

Note that after you make your first greegree, talismans can be purchased from Tutab's Magical Market for 1000 coins . Tutab will not open his shop unless you are in monkey form.

Note: This section is optional and not required for completing the quest, but it is required for future quests and it is convenient to do it now to save a future trip through the tunnels.

For the Recipe for Disaster quest, you will need an additional three greegrees (four in total). Each of these requires one talisman, for a total of four talismans plus their respective monkey bones if making all talismans in one go. You will save yourself several trips if you obtain all of these materials before going to Zooknock in the next section. You must kill one of each of the following:

Type: Karamjan monkey | Bones/corpse from:  | Quest: Monkey Madness I

Type: Ninja monkey | Bones/corpse from:  | Quest: Freeing King Awowogei

Type: Gorilla | Bones/corpse from:  | Quest: Freeing King Awowogei . Using melee is not recommended to fight the Monkey Guards , as they will indefinitely heal for 25 hitpoints when low health and in melee range. If using melee, you may get the guard to 26hp and then use poison or ranged to finish it off from a distance.

Type: Zombie monkey | Bones/corpse from:  | Quest: Freeing King Awowogei

Note : Some monkeys will have large and small variants; both will work for the quests, and merely change the size of your monkey form.

section_path: Monkey Business > Chapter 2 > Making the greegrees
text:
Once you have all of the required bones (or monkey corpse) and talismans, you must run through the tunnels again, bringing your items to Zooknock. Travel through the tunnel for a second time, and when you reach the end, use the monkey talisman and all monkey bones (or corpses) on Zooknock .

After a brief delay and conversation, you will get a greegree corresponding to the bones you used on him. To make another greegree, you have to first talk to him again and ask him if he can make another. If you cancel the conversation accidentally, ask how to make the monkey talisman and it will resume. If for some reason this doesn't work, try the drop trick with your previous greegrees, and go through the dialogue again. After all desired greegrees are made, bank or stock up as needed, and return to Ape Atoll .

''In which our hero/heroine finds himself/herself contending with life as a monkey.''

In this chapter, you will be required to speak with King Awowogei and retrieve a monkey from the Ardougne Zoo . If you need to bank or in order to be more efficient, you can skip to retrieving the monkey in Ardougne (section "Monkey See, Monkey Zoo" below), and then speak with Awowogei when you return to Ape Atoll (steps 1-3).

1- Wield the monkey greegree to become a monkey. In this form, you will not be approached or attacked by any of the monkeys or wildlife on the island, and you cannot engage in combat. As a Karamjan monkey, return to Garkor and speak with him. If you are transformed into a different kind of monkey, he'll tell you to change and come back. After you finish talking, with the m'speak amulet equipped, talk to the Elder Guard near Garkor. The guard will tell you to speak with Kruk .

2- From the guard, run west until you pass the main gate into Marim and have reached the Western shore of Ape Atoll (do not exit the gate). Head slightly south and follow the ground path up the western hill, then climb up the bamboo ladder at the top and cross the bamboo bridge. Climb down the ladder on the east side and speak to Kruk. After the conversation ends, he will conveniently take you back to King Awowogei .

3- Speak to Awowogei and offer an alliance, and he will ask you to rescue a monkey from the Ardougne Zoo . Teleport out and make your way to Ardougne.

section_path: Monkey Business > Chapter 3 > Monkey See, Monkey Zoo
text:
Once in Ardougne , ensure you have an empty inventory space and then head to the south-west corner and enter the zoo. Wield the greegree inside the zoo area to become a monkey, and then speak to the Monkey minder , who will place you in the cage. Speak with a monkey (the only one with a "Talk" option), and it'll hop into your inventory; then, unequip the greegree and speak to the Monkey minder again. He will be confused and let you out.

You will now need to travel by foot to the Gnome Stronghold . You cannot use any form of teleportation (including random events , spirit trees and fairy rings), as doing so will remove the monkey from your inventory, requiring you to re-obtain it from the zoo. The canoe system will work, however.

Once in the Gnome Stronghold , talk to Daero on the 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] to travel back to Ape Atoll as usual.

Extra: Your new monkey friend will supply you with some humorous dialogue, and examining him will get you poked. If you have any bananas in your inventory, he will most likely eat them. There is also a 1/256 chance that he will give you a clue scroll (medium) if you use bananas on him directly. These can be obtained conveniently from the trees in the Monkey Child 's garden or Solihib's Food Stall . Note that you must go through the entire dialogue. Only one clue may be obtained per player .

Once on Ape Atoll, equip your greegree and amulet to speak with Awowogei again. (If you have spoken before, simply speak to the Elder Guard to be let in; if not, refer to the section above). The monkey will automatically leave your backpack after speaking to Awowogei, and the king will consider an alliance.

Speak with Garkor to begin Chapter 4.

Speak with Garkor one more time (as a human or monkey) to receive a 10th squad sigil . Do not equip it until you are ready for the final battle . Make sure to hold onto the sigil, as if you lose it, Garkor will send you to Waymottin at the end of Zooknock 's tunnel to reclaim it.

Bank in preparation for the Jungle Demon fight, and ensure you have full prayer points and health. When you are ready to fight, wear the sigil, and you will be promptly teleported to the Jungle Demon's arena.

note:

You can wear the sigil, to start the fight, from anywhere in RuneScape; no need to return to Ape Atoll. Although you "wear" the sigil, it stays in your inventory and doesn't unequip your neck-slot equipment. Activate Protect from Magic before teleporting, and drink any necessary potions . Switch to your weapon/unequip your greegree before teleporting. You will lose your greegree if you have it equipped and your inventory is full when you teleport.

Upon landing in the arena, you'll be confronted by a level 195 Jungle Demon which can hit up to 32 with both magic and melee. Protection prayers reduce all damage to zero; as such, if the player stands out of melee range, the fight can be completed by simply leaving on Protect from Magic and attacking the demon with Magic or Ranged. Note that the demon's melee attack can hit you even if you're two squares away, similar to a halberd; ensure you're three or more squares away to avoid it. Additionally, standing still once you are teleported to the arena will keep a distance between you and the Demon, who will not move until you do, although it will still attack you with Magic.

similar to a halberd ; ensure you're three or more squares away to avoid it. additionally, standing still once you are teleported to the arena will keep a distance between you and the demon, who will not move until you do, although it will still attack you with magic.

The 10th Squad gnomes will be nearby to assist with the fight, but you must deal the final blow to the demon yourself. If the gnomes deal the final strike, he will heal around 20 percent of his health (anywhere from 12%-25%); when the demon reaches 1 hitpoint, there will be a period where the gnomes stop attacking, so use this window to deal the final blow yourself.

The demon is weakest to Ranged, although Magic is fairly effective. Players should focus on their combat style with the highest damage. Note that the dwarf multicannon is effective against the demon, allowing pure accounts to kill him without gaining any Hitpoints experience; additionally, despite being from the jungle, he is not immune to poison. Melee is not recommended, but players looking to use melee combat will benefit from using rings of recoil, as the demon's melee attacks hit very accurately.
There is a safespot in the arena, across a bridge on the outside edge. When you run to the safespot, he will make his way to the bridge, but won't be able to fit over it. You may run further down the outside edge to stop him from attacking at all, allowing you to wait for the 10th Squad to weaken him, then returning to the bridge to deal the final blow.

If you die during the fight, the sigil can be reclaimed from Death's Office. No need to run through the Ape Atoll Dungeon.

| Mission Over

The jingle that plays upon defeating the jungle demon.

Once the Jungle Demon is slain, speak to Garkor, who is indicated by an arrow. He will tell you to speak to Zooknock; speak to Zooknock nearby to get the option to be teleported back to Ape Atoll. If players decline the offer and stay, they are free to explore the banana plantation , but Zooknock will leave, requiring players to speak to Bonzara instead if they want to be teleported. He can be found in the crack at the base of the statue.

Warning : The gnomes will teleport you into the jungle on Ape Atoll. It is advised to simply teleport off of the island as quickly as possible; players wishing to stay on the island should immediately equip their greegree after being teleported by the gnomes.

Escape the island however you like, either through the main gates as a monkey, with any form of teleport, or by jumping off the bridge in the south-east part of the city, and go back to the Gnome Stronghold .

Speak with King Narnode in the Grand Tree to finish the quest.

Congratulations, quest complete!

The king will then redirect you to Daero for your training as a new 10th squad member, so go have a chat with Daero for some optional experience rewards.

3 Quest points 10,000 Coins 3 Diamonds Speaking to Daero after the quest gives the choice of either, 35,000 experience in Attack and Defence and 20,000 experience in Strength and Hitpoints OR 35,000 experience in Strength and Hitpoints and 20,000 experience in Attack and Defence . The skills you tell Daero you want to focus on will receive 35,000 XP each, and the others 20,000 each. Ability to buy and wield the Dragon scimitar (with level 60 Attack ) Full access to Ape Atoll, with the exception of the bank and javelin store, which are unlocked after Monkey Madness II .

After the quest, players retain the ability to turn into a monkey in Ape Atoll & Ardougne Zoo , using the Monkey greegree . The Jungle Demon can also now be fought in the Nightmare Zone . Note: while it was previously impossible to return to Ape Atoll after quest completion without receiving experience from Daero, an update in November 2022 now allows the training to be ignored before returning.

Lumo , Bunkdo , and Carado will make a random comment each time the player is captured and thrown back into jail, with special dialogue upon being caught 10, 15, 20, 50, and 100 times.

Additionally, the player will receive a stuffed monkey as a reward when being caught for the 100th time.

If you talk to Zeke , the scimitar seller of Al Kharid , and ask him for a Dragon scimitar , he will respond by saying, "The banana-brained nitwits who make them would never sell any to me.

Seriously, you'll be a monkey's uncle before you hold a Dragon Scimitar," referencing when you pretend to be a monkey's uncle to obtain the monkey talisman .

If you have started Fairytale II - Cure a Queen , completing this quest and receiving Daero's training unlocks a new fairy ring location in the Ape Atoll agility course .

This small area has two exits, one requires a ninja greegree , as well as 48 Agility to continue through the remainder of the agility course.

The other is a much slower route and crosses the nearby gorge by climbing the tower and crossing the rope bridge.

Description | The King of the northern Gnomes, Narnode Shareen, is once again in need of your help. He recently decided to send an envoy of his Royal Guard, the 10th squad, to oversee the decommissioning of the Gnome owned ship-building facilities on the eastern coast of Karamja . It has been quite some time since the 10th squad were dispatched and they have been deemed missing in action. It will be up to you, should you decide to help, to find out what fate befell the 10th squad and if possible, track them down. If only it were so simple. Sinister forces have begun to spread through the Gnome hierarchy and threaten to unleash an unknown terror upon the world. Far across the land, the fires of vengeance are being stoked once again. Can you unravel the mystery behind the deception? Can you separate the truth from the lies? Can you decide for yourself what is real and what is not?

text: Head to the Ardougne Zoo and equip your Karamjan monkey greegree , then talk to the Monkey minder . If you haven't talked to him before, click through his dialogue (ask any question), then equip the Karamjan monkey greegree . Equip your M'speak amulet and talk to a monkey, it will jump in your bag . Remove your greegree and talk to the minder again. Travel by foot (walk or run) back to the Grand Tree, then return to Ape Atoll by talking to Daero , Waydar , and Lumdo . Do not use any means of teleportation. Equip your M'speak amulet and Karamjan monkey greegree . Ape Atoll is no longer your enemy when wearing a greegree! If you want to skip going to talk to Kruk and you brought mithril seeds or tinderbox and logs you can stand on the east side of the Elder Guard and plant the mithril seeds or light a fire to be force moved one tile west and thus bypass needing to talk to Kruk or to Garkor . Follow the red path, go through the gates, then walk east to the coast and talk to Garkor . Talk to the nearby Elder Guard . Head to the west coast of the island (orange path), then climb up the hill to the south. Climb the ladder, walk across the bridge, climb down, and talk to Kruk . Talk to Awowogei . Talk to Awowogei again. Then talk to the Elder Guard again to be let out. Talk to Garkor and watch the cutscene. Talk to Garkor again to get the 10th squad sigil .

Prepare for final battle. Equip the 10th squad sigil when you are ready to fight the Jungle Demon . Tip: Use Protect from Magic prayer and stay out of melee range to avoid taking damage. Kill the Jungle Demon. Return to the Grand Tree and talk to King Narnode Shareen . Congratulations, quest complete!

An antipoison is a potion made by using unicorn horn dust on a marrentill potion (unf) , requiring 5 Herblore , yielding an antipoison(3) and 37.5 Herblore experience . A dose of antipoison cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds. Drinking two doses of antipoison will cure venom . The first dose will reduce the venom to poison and the second will remove the poison.

The next cheapest alternative, superantipoison , cures poison and provides immunity for 6 minutes.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , roe or caviar can be added to an antipoison(2), requiring 6 Herblore, yielding an antipoison mix and 12 Herblore experience. An antipoison mix has 2 doses, cures poison and provides immunity to poison for 90 seconds, and heals 3 Hitpoints .

An antipoison(1) spawn can be found in a chest in the Observatory Dungeon north-east of the stairs leading up to the Observatory . An antipoison(3) can be purchased from The Spice Is Right for 432 coins, Jiminua's Jungle Store for 432 coins, or 374 coins when wearing any tier of Karamja gloves . An antipoison(4) can be purchased from Apothecary's Potions in Varrock for 5 coins, a cadava berry , and a limpwurt root . An antipoison(4) is also a reward from Jekyll and Hyde random events if a marrentill is given to Dr Jekyll.

A banana is a type of food that restores 2 Hitpoints when eaten. It can be found on trees in tropical locations, such as Karamja and Ape Atoll , or bought from various stores. Six bananas can be picked at a time from  a banana tree grown by planting a banana sapling in a fruit tree patch with 33 Farming . They can also be obtained by using the spell Bones to Bananas , which converts bones of all types in the caster's inventory to bananas.

A single banana is required to cast the standard spellbook Ape Atoll Teleport with 64 Magic . The teleport can be added to a portal chamber or portal nexus , requiring 100 and 1,000 bananas respectively.

10 bananas are required for the Pirate's Treasure quest and 5 are required for Monkey Madness I . During the quest Tai Bwo Wannai Trio , a banana must be sliced using a knife or other sharp sword to create a sliced banana .

A basket of bananas can be created by using 1-5 bananas on an empty basket . Five full baskets of banana are required for a gardener to look after curry trees .

A banana is one of the three items retrieved from satchels obtained through the Creature Creation activity.

Birds are avian enemies found on Ape Atoll , Crash Island , inside the Nature Altar , in the Uzer Oasis , throughout the Isle of Souls , on the north coast of Aldarin , and in the southern Tlati Rainforest . They attack with melee and can be assigned as Slayer assignments by Turael . Although they are airborne, they use melee. When killed, they drop bones.

For the birds Slayer task, you can instead kill other birds such as chickens or mounted terrorbird gnomes .

A clue scroll (medium) is a valuable random drop from a large variety of mid-levelled monsters. Clue scrolls are the start of a Treasure Trail - a treasure hunt that sends players hunting all around Gielinor . At the end of the hunt players receive a reward of items randomly selected from a specific list, possibly including very rare and very valuable items. For a guide on how to complete a clue scroll, see: Treasure Trails Guide . Medium clue scrolls are mostly easy to obtain and complete, and offer average rewards in return. The rewards can range from mithril armour to ranger boots .

Medium clue scrolls can be between 3 and 5 steps long.

Medium clue scrolls offer coordinate clues along with more complex puzzles than easy clues, and occasionally a monster ranging from a chicken to a Market Guard may be fought. However, there are no clue steps that bring you to the Wilderness .

Completion of medium clues will give a casket (medium) containing the final reward for the trail. After completing 400 medium clues, the player will be awarded a clueless scroll .

Completion of Medium Combat Achievements gives a 5% increased chance to receive a medium clue scroll from all sources, excluding implings.

A medium clue scroll can be given to Watson along with an easy, hard and elite clue scrolls in order to receive a master clue scroll .

For players wishing to quickly obtain Medium clue scrolls, one of the best non-combat methods is thieving Aldarin Villa chests . While the clue drop rate from this chest is 1/90, the chest can be opened about 400 times per hour, yielding an average obtaining rate of one medium clue every 14 minutes or so, as well as ~80,000 Thieving experience per hour.

As clue scrolls are untradeable, they are sent to the gravestone if unprotected on PvP or PvM death, even above level 20 Wilderness . Clue boxes are not necessary and only add additional risk when in the Wilderness.

As with all tiers of clue scrolls, only one medium clue scroll can be held, kept in Death's Office, or stored in a bank at one time; attempting to open a scroll box (medium) while holding a medium clue scroll gives the message The clue box refuses to open - you already have a clue. However, it is possible to drop clues on the floor, where they'll stay for one hour, allowing players to have multiple clues at once. Dropping prior clue scrolls while having done some of their steps does NOT retain the steps of the dropped clue when starting a new one.

When casting an alchemy spell on a clue scroll, if the game setting that triggers a warning on untradeable items is disabled, a different confirmation warning is triggered, asking "wouldn't you rather solve the clue?". If the game setting is enabled, only the regular question is triggered.

Please note that it is possible to receive the same clue more than once.

Coins (also referred to as gold pieces , gp , gold , or simply money ) are the most common form of currency in Gielinor . They are used among players and non-player characters alike to exchange for items and services.

Players often refer to one thousand (1,000) coins as 1k and one million (1,000,000) coins as 1m or 1mil . Both can be applied to larger numbers, for example, 10m refers to ten million coins (10,000,000). 1b or 1bil refers to one billion coins (1,000,000,000).

Alchemy spells , which create coins, cannot be cast on coins. If a player attempts it, a message will inform the player that Coins are already made of gold. Curiously, other items made of gold, such as gold ore and gold bars , can be turned into coins with Alchemy spells.

Wearing a ring of wealth will automatically pick up coins dropped by NPCs upon killing them as long as the player has inventory space available.

Alternate terms for coins have seldom seen official usage since RuneScape Classic was replaced by RuneScape 2 . Very few NPCs use any other term than "coins," a few examples being the Blast Furnace foreman in Keldagrim , who calls them "GP", and the glassblower on Entrana , who calls them "gold pieces." The term "gp" is sometimes used in abbreviations such as on the right-click menu of the Al Kharid gates, which includes the option "Pay-toll(10gp)" to pay the toll and go through.

Some players purchase coins in exchange for real-world money through a third party. This is known as real world trading . Although players can potentially gain monetary value within RuneScape by such means, this method is not recommended, as Rule #12 of the RuneScape Code of Conduct forbids the trading of RuneScape items for items outside of RuneScape , and if engaged in can result in a player ban .

With the release of Old school bonds , however, players may acquire RuneScape coins using real-world money without breaching ToS, albeit indirectly, by buying bonds from Jagex and selling them in-game to other players or on the Grand Exchange .

Date: 25 June 2015 ( Update ) | Changes: Platinum tokens - stackable, tradeable items worth 1,000 coins each - were added. Players can use any bank booth, bank chest, or banker to convert one to the other.

RuneScape 2 Beta | 29 March 2004 – present

Coins appear in the inventory as plain flat discs, but during Grim Tales and in The Mimic fight, it is revealed that coins have more intricate designs imprinted on their faces. During the Shilo Village quest , there is an item that looks like coins in one of the tunnels that can only be picked up with Telekinetic Grab . These coins are non-stackable and untradeable. If a player tries to pick them up without Telekinetic Grab, they will be attacked and the coins will turn to dust. The maximum number of coins in a stack is 2,147,483,647, because RuneScape uses 32-bit signed integers to store values, which are unable to represent a higher number. A stack of this many coins is informally known as max cash . Players can ask Anja in Rimmington for some free stuff, and after the dialogue she will give 1 to 3 coins. There is a subdivision of coins in the lore called "coppers", unavailable to collect in game.

The dragon scimitar is the strongest scimitar available in Old School RuneScape . It can only be wielded by players who have 60 Attack and have completed the Monkey Madness I quest.

It may be purchased from Daga on Ape Atoll for 100,000 coins. A monkeyspeak amulet does not need to be worn, as players can just right-click 'Trade' on Daga; however, you still must be in monkey form , unless you have completed Monkey Madness II after which the monkey form is no longer required. Players who have freed King Awowogei in Recipe for Disaster can easily reach Marim through the Ape Atoll Teleport spell (requires 64 Magic ) to access Daga's shop on Ape Atoll quicker. The scimitar is also a rare drop from the Wilderness boss Scorpia or the Zombie Pirate's Locker .

As with most dragon equipment , the dragon scimitar cannot be made from raw materials using the Smithing skill.

One good alternative is the Arkan blade , which has very similar stats, the same 4-tick attack speed, and a great special attack, and is earned as a reward for completing The Final Dawn quest. This saves players the 100,000 coins used for purchasing the Dragon Scimitar.

The dragon scimitar has a special attack , Sever , costing 55% of the player's special attack energy and rolls against the target's slash defence with 25% higher accuracy. In PvP fights, this special attack has an additional effect that, upon a successful hit , disables the targeted player's active protection prayers ( Protect from Magic , Protect from Missiles , and Protect from Melee ) and prevents the targeted player from using said prayers for 8 ticks (4.8 seconds).

The dragon scimitar is one of the most easily attainable one-handed training weapons in the game. Its power is surpassed by weapons like the abyssal whip and the Ghrazi rapier . Due to whips and hastae being unable to solely train Strength, the dragon scimitar is often used to do so, and is therefore one of the most commonly used weapons in the game to train Strength.

It shares similar bonuses with Viggora's chainmace , with the chainmace being a crush weapon rather than a slash weapon .

Players can attach a dragon scimitar ornament kit or a Bounty Hunter ornament kit to cosmetically enhance the scimitar, creating a dragon scimitar (or) or dragon scimitar (cr) respectively. This only alters its appearance, and gives no stat enhancements. It can be dismantled, returning the scimitar and ornament kit.

The dragon scimitar was not actually released until almost four months after the release of the Monkey Madness I quest on 29 March 2005 . If the player asks Zeke to sell them a dragon scimitar before completing Monkey Madness I, he will say "Seriously, you'll be a monkey's uncle before you'll ever hold a dragon scimitar." The Dragon scimitar originally had a special attack that stopped your opponent from moving for a short period of time but Jagex later changed it in an update to stop protection prayers instead.

The enchanted bar is a quest item used during the Monkey Madness I quest. It is obtained by taking some monkey dentures , a gold bar and the m'amulet mould to Zooknock , the Royal Guard mage, at the end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon . After Monkey Madness II , it is impossible to reobtain this item, as Zooknock will just provide players with a completed m'speak amulet .

Zooknock will then infuse the magical powers of the dentures into the gold bar and return an enchanted bar. The player should then use this bar with the m'amulet mould on the magical flame in the dungeon below the temple to create an m'speak amulet .

Using the Listen option on the bar will result in hearing the voice of a monkey spirit, which can be understood if a m'speak amulet is worn.

An energy potion restores 15% of the player's run energy per dose. It can be made at level 26 Herblore by mixing a harralander in a vial of water and then adding chocolate dust , granting 67.5 Herblore experience.

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a 2 dose energy potion, which requires 29 Herblore and yields a 2 dose energy mix and 14 Herblore experience. An energy mix heals 3 hitpoints in addition to restoring 15% run energy.

Glough ( / ˈ ɡ l ʌ f / GLUFF ) is an ill-natured, misanthropic gnome who attempts to start a war against the humans . In The Grand Tree quest, he can be found in his house up a ladder just south-east of the ramp leading to the Grand Tree.

l ʌ f / gluff ) is an ill - natured, misanthropic gnome who attempts to start a war against the humans. in the grand tree quest, he can be found in his house up a ladder just south - east of the ramp leading to the grand tree.

Glough's schemes are thwarted in The Grand Tree quest, and once again in Monkey Madness I . He was originally the head tree guardian of the Tree Gnome Stronghold until his first plot was thwarted by the player. He makes his first unsuccessful attempt on the player's life when he summons a black demon to kill them in The Grand Tree, and is indirectly responsible for the second attempt in Monkey Madness I, where he provides a powerful spell and a Jungle Demon to Awowogei , which is used in an attempt to trap the 10th Squad , but is defeated by the player. During Monkey Madness II , the player manages to break the alliance between Glough and the monkeys by sabotaging Awowogei 's forces, along with his alliance between the ogres and trolls. Becoming increasingly deranged and desperate, Glough launches an attack on the Grand Tree by himself. He eventually meets his end at the hands of the player after a great skirmish, but not before killing Nieve .

King Narnode Shareen sends a human adventurer on a mission to discover why the Grand Tree is dying. Little do they know that the wheels of Glough's dreams of world domination and hatred of humans have been put in motion, and is in the process of preparing an armada of warships to strike at the heart of the human kingdoms.

In The Grand Tree, players discover that Glough has hired a man named Charlie to steal the Daconia rocks —magic stones kept by one of the original creators of the Grand Tree, Hazelmere , that can be used to wound and even kill the Grand Tree in the event that it went out of control—so that he can frame him as the one who is responsible for the dying Grand Tree. Glough has used these rocks on the roots of the Grand Tree to wound it and eventually kill it, so the wood from the tree can be used to construct battleships. In framing Charlie, he attempts to convince King Narnode that humans are trying to destroy the Grand Tree, which the King initially believes, so Narnode prepares for war against the human kingdoms.

The adventurer eventually finds evidence of Glough's culpability in these plans and discovers that Glough has contracted workers to construct large warships in a distant Ship Yard to invade the human territories and attempt to control the world. After presenting this evidence to the King and following an investigation of Glough's estate by the King's subjects, the King explains that all they found were a couple of sticks. When the player deciphers the meaning of these sticks and takes them to their intended area, the adventurer finds themselves entrapped by Glough who sets a black demon on them. The adventurer kills the demon, prompting Glough to flee. He is eventually discovered by the King and his guards, and the adventurer discovers the remaining daconia rocks. Under the weight of all of this evidence, King Narnode has Glough placed under house arrest and cancels the invasion.

Meanwhile, an angry Glough plots his revenge against the adventurer.

King Narnode sends the adventurer to investigate the disappearance of the elite 10th squad , who were tasked with decommissioning the Ship Yard where Glough was preparing an armada to attack mankind. It turns out that the 10th Squad crashed on a small island south of Karamja due to powerful winds that damaged their gliders. When most of the squad leaves the island to inspect a nearby atoll that had been spotted prior to the crash, several of them are captured by sentient apes who imprison them. Some of the 10th squad successfully escape, while two conduct espionage and three others work on carrying out a rescue operation for those captured.

When Daero gives the adventurer a puzzle box to solve, the adventurer can alternatively bring it to Glough to have him solve it for them. However, Glough will charge the player 200,000 coins before nearly completing the puzzle for them, not completing it as it would have set off an alarm.

In Monkey Madness I, the adventurer discovers that G.L.O. Caranock is continuing Glough's plans for warfare with the humans in his absence. King Awowogei , the leader of the apes, is eventually found to be conspiring with Glough's henchmen to attack mankind. By utilising a powerful spell provided by Glough, they will be able to teleport all of the 10th squad to an arena with an enormous Jungle Demon to have them killed off. Fortunately, the squad commander, Sergeant Garkor , learns of their intent before they act on it, and with a bit of ingenuity, enables the player to teleport with the 10th squad when it happens. The demon is defeated, and it appears that Caranock's and Awowogei's plans are foiled for the time being.

After Monkey Madness I, Glough can still be found in his treehouse, and when spoken to, says, " Mark my words, the monkeys are listening ". This is a hint towards the Monkey Madness II quest.

Glough mysteriously disappears from house arrest, which prompts King Narnode to send the player to find out what he is plotting. It is soon revealed that Assistant Le Smith had smuggled him out of house arrest and dropped him off at Ape Atoll.

Glough has been experimenting with the monkeys and gorillas of Ape Atoll with an unknown mutagen. Awowogei was unaware of this, and had simply labelled it as Kruk 's "secret weapon". When the adventurer arrives on Glough's airship disguised as Kruk, Glough tells them to send the remaining three tortured gorillas back into their cages, as they had broken out. After the gorillas are thrown back into the cage, Glough tells them that the mutagen is almost perfect, and that he is aiming to create a mutagen that makes the applicant more aggressive, but obedient to the controller. He leaves the adventurer to find Le Smith; the adventurer quickly sabotages the onyx charging the mutagen.

After finding Le Smith, Glough hears about the monkeys backing off their attack. Despite this, he still continues onward. While on the airship, the tormented gorillas break out and crash the ship. Glough manages to survive the crash and takes his best "experiments" into a cavern . When the adventurer and Nieve arrive, Glough realises that the player had been foiling his plans all along, and sends two tortured and demonic gorillas at them; however, the player and Nieve are able to defeat them. Glough becomes angered and drinks the remaining mutagen to finish off the adventurer and Nieve. Nieve attempts to stop Glough, but the mutated Glough slams her into a wall and stomps the ground, causing a boulder to crash and kill Nieve.

After a long battle between the mutated Glough and the adventurer, Glough is eventually defeated. However, the cavern becomes increasingly unstable due to Glough's actions and collapses, presumably killing him.

A gold bar is a bar of refined gold created through the Smithing skill at level 40 by using a gold ore with a furnace , or by casting Superheat Item on it. By default, this gives 22.5 Smithing experience per bar, but if the goldsmith gauntlets from the Family Crest quest are worn, the experience given is boosted to 56.2.

The primary use of gold bars is to create jewellery through the Crafting skill. To craft gold bars into jewellery, players must use a gold bar on a furnace with the proper mould in their inventory . If players wish to craft jewellery with gems inset, they must also have the respective cut gems.

Gorilla bones are the bones dropped by the level 167 Monkey Guards that inhabit the Temple of Marimbo on Ape Atoll .

Zooknock is able to make a gorilla greegree with the bones in the Ape Atoll Dungeon. If players want to make a bearded gorilla greegree , they must use bearded gorilla bones instead. After completion of Monkey Madness II , players no longer need to bring bones; they can simply claim the greegree from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold .

Gorilla bones give 18 Prayer experience when buried. This can be increased by offering the bones in different ways:

The Jungle Demon is a quest monster fought during the Monkey Madness I quest. It is among the strongest demons in the game. It uses extremely strong magic attacks, and when in range, a halberd -like melee attack. It is possible to stand to the side and let the gnomes spawned around the jungle demon lower its hitpoints down to 10 (players wishing to use this method should hide across the bridge at the edge of the arena ). Afterwards, player can run out to quickly finish it off. However, if the gnomes "kill" the demon, it will restore 12-25% of its hitpoints, so you cannot fully rely on the 10th Squad to kill it. Players might also find it difficult to deal the final-blow depending on their combat level, leading to the demon restoring its hitpoints multiple times. Activate Protect from Magic, and drink any necessary potions , before entering the fight.

The Jungle Demon alternates between all four wave spells for its magic attacks, and its melee attack is like a halberd (which means that it can hit two tiles away). Both types of attacks can hit up to 32 damage.

It can be fought in the Nightmare Zone after the quest is complete.

Like all demons, it is susceptible to the effects of demonbane weapons .

It is recommended that players bring 2-3 four dose prayer potions depending on their Prayer level (37 for Protect from Magic makes the fight considerably easier). Without Protect from Magic, a high magic defence and lots of food may be required. The rest of your inventory should have monkfish or better, as well as magic or ranging equipment, depending on your method of attack. A single-click teleport can also be helpful in emergencies.

Bank in preparation for the Jungle Demon fight, and ensure you have full prayer points and health. When you are ready to fight, wear the sigil (you can do this from anywhere; no need to return to Ape Atoll), and you will be promptly teleported to the Jungle Demon's arena. Activate Protect from Magic before teleporting, and drink any necessary potions .

The easiest way to kill the Jungle Demon is to hide at the edge of the arena, waiting until the gnomes get him down to about 10 hitpoints. Afterwards, you can run out and finish it quickly. The Jungle Demon will regenerate to 20% of its full health if you do not deal the final blow. Note that the demon's melee attack can hit you even if you're two squares away, similar to a halberd; ensure you're three or more squares away to avoid it. Additionally, standing still once you are teleported to the arena will keep distance between you and the Demon, who will not move until you do, although it will still attack you with Magic.

For those without 37 Prayer, the above method is highly recommended. Be sure to equip high magic defence gear and farcast it using Ranged or Magic spells. Alternatively, a dragon dagger special attack can be used four times in a row, which is very likely to knock it out as well.

Those with 37 Prayer can simply attack the Jungle Demon from a distance by either using Ranged or Magic spells while using the Protect from Magic prayer.

Using a dwarf multicannon , fewer than twenty (20) steel cannonballs may be used, making the cannon the most effective way to kill the demon.

Although most demons are very weak to Magic, the Jungle Demon has a high magic level and high magic defence, so using Magic against it is not recommended. To avoid the demon continually healing when using magic, wait for the gnomes to get the demon to 15-20 hitpoints, then use Protect from Magic and run across the arena to another bridge. The gnomes won't follow, so you don't have to worry about the demon healing while your magic splashes.

Kruk is a commander monkey and the captain of the Monkey Guard, a unit of sword-wielding ninja monkeys . He is located in Marim on Ape Atoll , atop the cliff east of the entry gates, which he shouts to be opened when the player (in their monkey form) approaches. Despite having a combat level, he cannot be attacked until a certain stage in Monkey Madness II , nor does he attack the player if they unequip their greegree ; he simply knocks them unconscious instead and transports them to the Marim jail.

To reach Kruk, go up the incline on the west cliff (there is a fenced opening). Head to the ladder at the end, cross the bridge, and go down the other ladder. He is bigger than the other ninja monkeys. Duke replaces Kruk during and after the events of Monkey Madness II.

Kruk plays a minor role in Monkey Madness I . The player must speak to him to be escorted to King Awowogei and continue the quest.

In Monkey Madness II , the player, after successfully navigating through Kruk's Dungeon , defeats him and takes his paw to make a Kruk greegree . It is then revealed that Kruk has been secretly helping Glough with his experiments , capturing monkeys for him to use as specimens. When the player, impersonating Kruk, informs Awowogei of the failed plans that they sabotaged, he strips Kruk of his ranks and duties and later replaces him with Duke .

It is possible to safespot and kill Kruk with minimal to no damage by flinching him with melee. Lure Kruk north-west against the cave wall, then run behind the corner.

When being fought, Kruk's melee and ranged attacks are very powerful, capable of dealing 30+ damage each.

A m'speak amulet is an item crafted during Monkey Madness I that allows the player to communicate with monkeys . It is later used in the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest as well as Monkey Madness II . After completion of Monkey Madness II, the amulet is no longer needed to speak with monkeys (though the amulet is no longer used after Chapter III of the quest).

To make one, the player must take monkey dentures , a m'amulet mould , and a gold bar to Zooknock , who will give them an enchanted bar (and the mould back). They must then use the bar on the wall of flame in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon with the mould in their inventory to create an unstrung m'speak amulet . The amulet can be completed using a ball of wool or the String Jewellery spell.

If the m'speak amulet is lost, it can be reobtained by repeating the above steps, or if Monkey Madness II has been completed, by speaking with Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold .

Since Zooknock returns the m'amulet mould to the player when the bar is created, only one mould is required to create two or more enchanted bars.

Stringing the amulet displays the message You put some string on your amulet. It makes a slight 'Ook' sound.

Mithril seeds are a magical type of seed that can be planted almost anywhere to grow some flowers in the ground, and are purchasable from the Legends Guild Shop of Useful Items.

Upon planting the seeds, the player will move one adjacent square west if possible; if there's an obstacle preventing movement to the west, the flowers will attempt to move the player to the east first, then south, then north. Once the flower is grown, players are then given the option to pick them, producing one of nine different colours of flowers .

Mithril seeds are primarily used in PvP activities in the Wilderness , or in minigames such as Last Man Standing , as it forces the user to move one tile even if the player is frozen. Adamant seeds , a variant of the item, will move the opposite direction from mithril seeds.

Seeds are sometimes used to grief players training Hunter and Firemaking as well, as traps and fires cannot be placed on the same tile as a planted flower.

40 seeds are awarded upon completion of the Waterfall Quest . Players can buy them at the Legends' Guild .

The monkey is a talkative animal obtained during the Monkey Madness I quest. Unlike other animals in-game, it stays in your inventory rather than following you around.

Using any form of teleportation will cause the monkey to vanish. The monkey cannot be banked.

If you drop the monkey, it wanders around for about 30 seconds before disappearing, during which time it can be picked up again by talking to it. However, if the monkey is dropped on Karamja , it becomes a monster like other Karamjan monkeys and exclaims "Yay! I'm free!," granting the player Thieving experience equal to twice their level before disappearing.

While in your inventory, the monkey can be poked, much to its annoyance, and it will often interrupt the player with forced dialogue. It can be fed bananas , monkey nuts , monkey bars , and banana stew , although it will claim to not want the latter items, despite eating them anyway. The monkey will also occasionally eat bananas in your inventory without notice.

During the Monkey Madness I quest, the player is tasked with saving a monkey from the Ardougne Zoo in order to earn the trust of the monkey king Awowogei . The monkey can only be obtained by wielding a Karamjan monkey greegree and talking to the Monkey Minder , who will put you in the cage with the other monkeys. Once in the cage, talk to a monkey with an m'speak amulet equipped and convince the monkey to get into your backpack.

To get out of the cage, unequip the greegree and speak with the Monkey Minder, who will remove you from the cage.

You can obtain a one-off medium clue scroll from the monkey by manually feeding it bananas . The chance of receiving the clue scroll is 1/256, and when it occurs, a message will appear in the chatbox saying The monkey chews on the banana and spits out a clue. .

In order to trigger the chance of receiving the clue scroll, you must click "Click here to continue" on the dialogue that appears each time you feed the monkey.

Once you've obtained a clue scroll from the monkey, feeding it will result in a message saying The monkey is grateful, but it won't give you any more clues. .

Monkey Guards are level 167 gorillas that reside in the Temple of Marimbo , found on Ape Atoll . They reside on the ground floor [ UK ] 1 st floor [ US ] and 1 st floor [ UK ] 2 nd floor [ US ] of Ape Atoll 's Temple of Marimbo and are the strongest guard found on Ape Atoll. They have a large amount of health and throw vicious punches that can hit up to 14. When they have very low health, they will beat their chest, causing them to heal 25 hitpoints , which is about 20% of their maximum health; they appear to be able to do this indefinitely but only while in melee range. Monkey Guards drop larger versions of monkey bones, which give 18 prayer experience points when buried. However, these are not tradeable.

Bearded monkey guards can be a nuisance because they cannot be walked through. After exiting the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon , bearded Monkey Guards can block the player from exiting the temple. Either wait or climb up the ladder near the trapdoor.

There is a way, however, to kill the Monkey Guards (including bearded variants) using melee as a player with relatively low combat stats. Monkey Guards can be brought down to 26-35 HP by normal attacks. The player can then poison the Monkey Guard using a Dragon dagger(p++) or other super-poisoned weapon. Once the Monkey Guard is poisoned, and before the Monkey Guard heals, the player can run out of range of the poisoned Monkey Guard, and wait for the poison damage to finish him off. The south-western corner of the Monkey Guard temple is a good place to poison and safespot one of the Monkey Guards, as there is a ladder that the player can hide behind. They still use their healing ability when being flinched , however. Alternatively, you can safespot them and use ranged to easily kill them as they won't use their healing ability when they can't attack you.

It is possible to utilise the stairs near the prayer altar to bypass the healing, though this technique is precise and tedious. Further, the monkey guard may not cooperate by wandering away while you are on the second floor. Best done with a 4 tick weapon.

A monkey talisman is used for making greegrees until the completion of Monkey Madness II . When taken to Zooknock along with the corresponding materials, he will enchant it into a greegree.

It is first acquired by talking to the Monkey Child on Ape Atoll while wearing a M'speak amulet . The talismans sold at Tutab's Magical Market may only be bought after Zooknock enchants the original, or the player can get another one for free from the monkey child.

To make a greegree, the player must kill any type of monkey (excluding a skeleton monkey ), pick up the bones, and bring them with the monkey talisman to Zooknock at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon . To get there, go down the ladder south of the atoll and follow the long and dangerous tunnel to the other end of the dungeon. It is strongly recommended that players have level 43 Prayer for Protect from Melee . It is also a good idea to bring prayer potions and/or energy potions . After Monkey Madness II, Zooknock will give talismans without the need for bones and will be located in the Gnome Stronghold

Note: There are nine greegrees in total, but only seven of them require bones; the four other monkeys that can be killed for bones are monkey archers , ninja monkey guards , monkey zombies , and gorilla monkey guards . The two exceptions are the ancient gorilla and Kruk monkey greegrees, which require the monkey skull or Kruk's paw , respectively.

During Monkey Madness I , the monkey child asks for 20 bananas in exchange for a monkey talisman, but the player only has to give him 4-10 because he can't count. To get another talisman after that, they must talk to him again. The player will tell him that they lost it, and he will start to cry. They can either log out of the game or wait for around a minute (watch out for the Monkey's Aunt or use a greegree) and then he will cheer up, allowing them to take another one. This can be done as many times as needed.

An excellent strategy is to get all greegree types after acquiring the first (the Karamjan monkey greegree ). With the greegree equipped, sneak up behind any monkey, then quickly change back into human form to attack it. This way, all damage is avoided until the player reaches the monkey. Bring decent gear, food , antipoison potions , and prayer potions for protection prayers . If killing a monkey guard, players can recharge their prayer points by praying at the gorilla statue .

Be advised that greegrees may not be equipped while in combat.

A Prayer potion is a potion made by using snape grass on a ranarr potion (unf) , requiring 38 Herblore , yielding a Prayer potion(3) and 87.5 Herblore experience . A dose of Prayer potion restores Prayer points equal to 7 + 25% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. If a Prayer cape , Max cape or ring of the gods (i) is equipped or a Prayer cape , Max cape or holy wrench is in the player's inventory, the restore increases to 7 + 27% of the player's current Prayer level, rounded down. It provides less Prayer point restoration than a super restore potion by 1 point per dose.

Prayer potions are always in high demand due to use of Prayers during combat or skilling activities and a need to restore points without travelling to an altar .

After Barbarian Herblore Training , caviar can be added to a Prayer potion(2), requiring 42 Herblore, yielding a Prayer mix and 29 Herblore experience. A Prayer mix has 2 doses, restores Prayer by the same amounts, and heals 6 Hitpoints , with the disadvantage being it now incurs an attack delay.

The ring of dueling is a teleportation ring that may be made by casting Lvl-2 Enchant on an emerald ring , granting 37 Magic experience. A full ring of dueling will provide 8 teleports before it crumbles away into nothing.

When teleporting using the ring, the message You rub the ring... will be displayed, followed by a message with the number of charges remaining, ex. Your ring of dueling has four uses left. If using the last charge on the ring, the message Your ring of dueling crumbles to dust. will be displayed instead.

Due to the low cost of the ring, many players use it to bank quickly at the Castle Wars chest. Furthermore, the Ferox Enclave teleport allows a player to use the Pool of Refreshment whilst gaining full health, prayer and run energy, although the Ferox Enclave teleport places the player slightly farther away from a bank chest.

Each charge costs 108.63 coins if all 8 charges are used, 34.43 if using High Level Alchemy (as described below), or 70.86 if using Low Level Alchemy . Alternatively, Explorer's ring can be used 30 times per day for a cost of 51.29 . This is viable if fewer than 210 charges are used on average each day, though it gives no Magic experience.

The ring of life is a diamond ring that has been enchanted with Lvl-4 Enchant . While worn, if the wearer is attacked and has 10% or less of their Hitpoints remaining, the ring automatically teleports the wearer to their respawn point . The ring crumbles to dust after one use. A Defence cape can be worn for the same effect, which does not destroy itself on activation. An Escape crystal can be configured to provide the same effect and more.

The ring does not guarantee total safety, as a player wearing one will still die if they are hit from above 10% of their maximum Hitpoints to zero (for example, being hit 15 while at 15 hitpoints), and it will not cure poison . Self-inflicted damage, such as guzzling a dwarven rock cake or using a locator orb , can also activate the effect. If it is worn along with a phoenix necklace , the necklace effect will trigger first. In PvP , the Tele Block spell will prevent a player's ring of life from activating.

It is one the few items whose teleports will work up to level 30 Wilderness, while most other means of teleportation will not work above level 20 Wilderness.

In Wintertodt , the ring will activate if warmth drops below 10%.

Upon the completion of medium Ardougne Diary , the teleport destination can be toggled to East Ardougne .

When the ring of life effect procs, a player wearing the ring of life will be teleported and the following chat message will appear: Your Ring of Life saves you and is destroyed in the process.

Skeletons are undead gorillas found in the multi-combat Ape Atoll Dungeon . Players are required to run past them during the Monkey Madness I quest in order to reach Zooknock . Players are advised to use Protect from Melee against these monsters, as they attack accurately and can easily overwhelm with their sheer numbers. They are aggressive to all players who are not using a greegree to turn themselves into a monkey.

Their special respawn mechanics tendency to cluster around a player means that they are often a popular choice for players training Ranged or Magic . Players who have access to maniacal monkeys should kill them instead as these skeletons do not have any drops to mitigate supply costs.

If the bones dropped by a skeletal gorilla are left on the ground for too long, another skeletal gorilla will emerge from them. After 10 ticks (6 seconds) upon killing a skeletal gorilla, all suitable bones within a 5x5 tile square centred on the player will be reanimated, spawning a skeleton lasting for just under two minutes before crumbling down again. If there are too many skeletal gorillas already spawned, they instead turn into "burning bones", which cannot be picked up.

When they respawn, they do so with a unique animation of them coming out of the ground. The bones cannot be taken away from Ape Atoll , and when teleporting out, a message appears saying The skeleton bones you are carrying crumble to dust . Ashes are then left in your inventory.

A stamina potion restores 20% of the player's run energy per dose, and offers a 70% reduction in run energy depletion for 2 minutes. This effect does not stack, and drinking additional doses before the timer has run out will simply reset it back to 2 minutes. When the stamina effect is active, the boost in the run energy orb changes from its usual yellow to orange.

A stamina potion can be made at level 77 Herblore by mixing a super energy potion with amylase crystals . Each dose grants 25.5 Herblore experience , and requires one amylase crystal.

At 85 Herblore, they can be used to make extended stamina potions using marlin scales .

After Barbarian Herblore Training is completed, caviar can be added to a stamina potion(2) to produce a stamina mix . This requires 86 Herblore and provides 60 Herblore experience. A stamina mix has 2 doses, each healing 6 Hitpoints in addition to the usual stamina potion behaviour.

Stamina potions are extremely useful in activities that require a lot of running. With a low enough weight , the reduced energy depletion will result in minimal loss of energy even with non-stop running, especially combined with the 20% restoration when taking another dose.

The relevance of stamina potions diminished with the 2025 Run Energy Changes update, as run energy drain was decreased across the board. However, the impact of the stamina potion effect on energy drain is still significant, and stamina potions remain relevant at some activities.

Common uses for stamina potions include: questing , player killing , Blast Furnace , hunting the Herbiboar , runecrafting , some Agility courses (e.g., Ape Atoll ), and raiding at the Theatre of Blood . They are also used to build a revitalisation pool as well as charge the ring of endurance , with each dose granting one charge for the ring.

Due to their high Herblore requirement, ironmen cannot make them until much later in their account progression. For this reason, there are several methods of obtaining stamina potions that are used.

Stamina potions can be obtained by giving torstol to Dr Jekyll when he appears. Due to the rarity of the event, players often save up ten staminas to build the revitalisation pool in their player-owned house , which requires 70 Construction . Outside of obtaining it through monster drops, players without the Farming level to grow torstol can obtain it from the Wintertodt Reward Cart , the dark chest on the Isle of Souls , or the Sinister chest in the Yanille Agility Dungeon . Players lacking the required level to clean Torstol can have Zahur clean their grimy herbs; alternatively, clean Torstol can also be obtained from Zulrah or Nature implings .

While Dr Jekyll normally despawns if a player runs into a bank, several locations (typically those without a booth) are exempt from this. Examples include the banks on Lunar Isle , in the Myths' Guild , and at the Theatre of Blood . Players lucky enough to be near those locations when he spawns can use this to grab a torstol from the bank, if they have one. An unprepared player may minigame teleport to Last Man Standing and speak to the Banker to withdraw a banked herb with a few seconds to spare.

Dr Jekyll has a higher chance to spawn when Underwater because the pool of random events is smaller. Players can deliberately farm stamina potions by spending time underwater when a random event would typically occur.

Players with friends capable of carrying them through the Pestilent Bloat and Maiden fights of the Theatre of Blood will gain access to a chest which contains one 4-dose stamina potion. This requires completion of Priest in Peril , meaning that skillers cannot use this method.

Summer pie is a type of pie with two bites that restores 11 Hitpoints , 10% run energy , and grants a +5 temporary skill boost to Agility per bite. A pie dish will remain after consumption.

It can be created by baking a raw summer pie on a cooking range , requiring level 95 Cooking and granting 260 experience when successful. When cooking there is a chance to fail, resulting in burnt pie . The burn rate decreases as the player's Cooking level increases. Summer pies never stop burning altogether even at level 99, unless the player is wearing a Cooking cape . Alternatively, casting the Bake Pie spell from the lunar spellbook will always create a pie without burning it.

Summer pies are a type of 1 tick (0.6 seconds) fast food , meaning you can eat them in succession with less delay than standard food which adds a 3-tick (1.8 second) penalty. Because of this short eat delay, summer pies can restore health quicker than manta rays , making them more efficient for healing up a lot of lost health in the same amount of ticks. However, as each half adds 3 ticks of attack delay, they are less efficient in combat than other high-healing foods.

The +5 Agility boost makes summer pies a great food for use in Agility training, increasing the chance to pass obstacles while restoring Hitpoints lost from failing any. It may also be used to pass Agility level requirements in quests , Agility courses , shortcuts or any other activities with an Agility requirement . Not all requirements can be boosted, such as Dragon Slayer II , the Ape Atoll Agility Course or Saradomin's Encampment in the God Wars Dungeon . The Preserve prayer may be used to extend the duration of the boost.

Summer pies are popular for fighting the Chaos Elemental or Chaos Fanatic as the empty pie dish prevents their special attacks from un-equipping Worn Equipment due to a full inventory.

Successfully baking a summer pie inside of the Cooks' Guild is an elite Varrock Diary task.

The small zombie monkey greegree is used for transforming into a small zombie monkey on Ape Atoll . To make one, a player must either take a monkey talisman and small zombie monkey bones to Zooknock at the very end of the Ape Atoll Dungeon (pre Monkey Madness II ), or get one for free from Zooknock in the Tree Gnome Stronghold (post Monkey Madness II). Materials are not required if Monkey Madness II has been completed.

There are two different zombie greegrees. This type is made using bones from the level 82 monkey zombies in the Temple of Marimbo Dungeon . While transformed, a player can use the wall of flame to create an uncut zenyte and may walk safely across the bed of hot rocks in the dungeon. The player cannot run while transformed into a zombie monkey.

A glitch exists where if the player gets caught and they try to transform back, there is a small chance they will lose their greegree; however, this glitch is not common. If the player has a full inventory, and teleports from Ape Atoll without removing their greegree, they will lose it.

Either size greegree can be used in completing the Recipe for Disaster Awowogei subquest.
